title: Ataxia due to vitamin E deficiency: A case report and updated review
case_prompt:
A 16-year-old boy was referred for evaluation of progressive gait difficulties and generalized weakness that began at age 10. He reported associated muscle wasting and slurred speech. His birth history was unremarkable, and there was no family history of neurologic disease, consanguinity, or gastrointestinal symptoms.

On examination, he had a broad-based, ataxic gait, tongue fasciculations, intentional tremor, and dysdiadochokinesia. Upper and lower limb strength was 3/5, deep tendon reflexes were absent, and ankle clonus was present. Sensory examination, cranial nerves, and cognitive function were normal. There was no head titubation or additional abnormal movements. General systemic examination, including cardiovascular and pulmonary assessments, was unremarkable.

Routine blood chemistries, electrocardiography, echocardiography, and brain MRI were reported as normal. Ophthalmologic evaluation showed only simple myopia. Laboratory studies revealed a vitamin A level of 45 mcg/dL (normal 20–60) and a vitamin E level of 3.9 mg/dL (normal 6–10). Creatine kinase was 80 mcg/L (normal 10–120). Other tests—including full blood count, glucose, liver and kidney function, coeliac antibodies, fasting lipids, thyroid function, copper, and ceruloplasmin—were within normal limits. Genetic analysis of the frataxin gene showed two alleles in the normal size range with no evidence of expansion.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Friedreich ataxia was initially considered because of the childhood-onset progressive ataxia but was excluded when genetic testing showed no frataxin-gene expansions “Genetic analysis of the frataxin gene confirmed two alleles in the normal size range and no evidence of an expansion.”  
2. Abetalipoproteinemia was considered as a cause of hereditary vitamin E deficiency but was excluded by the absence of gastrointestinal symptoms and a normal lipid profile “Other laboratory investigations confirmed ... fasting lipids ... normal.”
final_diagnosis: Ataxia with isolated vitamin E deficiency
